reading.body:
J-Curve Technologies is not a confirmed data center: no operator, website, business registration, or press coverage could be found for the Tempe, Arizona address, and no power specifications are published.

The entry is a mapped point, not a verified facility. Reverse geocoding of the stored coordinates returns only a building at 2005 West 14th Street, Tempe, with no business name attached, and the name itself is more common in finance than in the technology industry. Research status is exhausted and specifications are unpublished. The address sits more than 20 miles from other rows in the same batch, so no single shared building links them.

For AI scaling, the useful number is Arizona's: 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish power specifications, totaling 512 MW. Any estimate of Arizona grid load from data centers rests on those four. The other 52, this one included, cannot be ranked or counted, because nothing about their capacity is public.

What this does not say is that the building has no servers. It says the operator cannot be confirmed and the load cannot be measured. It also gives no statewide capacity figure, only the count of facilities and the small subset that disclose power. A map of data centers and a map of data center demand are not the same map.
